scenes.title: Chicken claw vs snow scene: left hand points at the snow shovel while the mouth invents an excuse

layout.description: Bright mid-century psychology laboratory where a seated split-brain patient fixes his gaze on a central black dot on a frosted rear-projection tachistoscope screen; a snow-covered house flashes on the left half and a chicken claw flashes on the right half while his left hand points down at a snow-shovel picture card and his right hand points at a chicken card on the wooden table.

positions.who: Split-brain patient (mannequin in 1960s collared cardigan shirt)
positions.where: seated center at the wooden testing table facing the central fixation dot on the screen
positions.facing: staring dead ahead at the fixation cross while pointing with both hands

positions.who: Neuroscientist Michael Gazzaniga (mannequin in 1960s white shirt and narrow tie)
positions.where: standing camera-right beside the rear-projection screen with a notepad
positions.facing: observing both pointing hands and listening to the spoken excuse

positions.where: operating the high-speed slide shutter behind the frosted screen

props.name: dual-field frosted tachistoscope screen
props.period_detail: back-lit glass projection panel with central fixation dot flashing a wintry snow scene on the left and a chicken claw on the right for 100 milliseconds
props.physical_behavior: flashes both images briefly then returns to blank white

props.name: row of eight printed choice cards on the table
props.period_detail: matte cardboard cards including a snow shovel on the left and a rooster/chicken on the right
props.physical_behavior: patient's left index finger taps the snow-shovel card while his right index finger taps the chicken card

props.name: 1960s slide projector with rapid mechanical timer
props.period_detail: brushed-metal laboratory projector behind the screen

actions.verb_sequence: keeps eyes fixed on the center dot as snow and claw flash -> points left hand firmly onto the snow-shovel card and right hand onto the chicken card -> gestures conversationally as he explains the chicken shed
points to the patient's left hand on the snow shovel -> tilts head in amazement at the instant spoken rationalization

reactions.reaction: nods with complete calm confidence, utterly unaware his speaking half never saw the snow
writes rapidly on his clipboard, stunned by the seamless post-hoc story

scenes.wardrobe: 1960s collegiate button-down shirt and knit cardigan on patient; white dress shirt and narrow dark tie on Gazzaniga.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key 1960s laboratory daylight balanced with the bright tachistoscope panel.
scenes.recognition_hook: His left hand points to a snow shovel and his right hand points to a chicken — and his speaking left brain smoothly invents a story about cleaning out a chicken shed.

key_visual.description: the split-brain patient stares at the alternating matched-angle while his left hand points to a snow shovel card and his right hand points to a chicken card

scenes.title: Intermanual conflict: left hand unbuttons what the right hand buttons
scenes.era: 1962 postwar California home of Patient W.J.

layout.description: Sunlit 1960s bedroom mirror area where Patient W.J. tries to button his dress shirt while his own left hand reaches up to undo the buttons.

positions.where: standing before a bedroom dresser buttoning his shirt
positions.facing: looking down at his competing hands

props.name: 1960s white button-down shirt
props.period_detail: cotton dress shirt with plastic front buttons
props.physical_behavior: right fingers fasten a button while left fingers pull the button back open

actions.verb_sequence: fastens the middle shirt button with his right hand -> his left hand rises and unbuttons it -> his right hand grabs his left wrist

reactions.reaction: stares down at his own rebellious left hand in disbelief

scenes.wardrobe: 1960s white cotton dress shirt and dark trousers.
scenes.recognition_hook: After callosotomy, his left hand literally unbuttoned the shirt his right hand was trying to put on.

scenes.title: 'I saw nothing' — yet the left hand grabs the exact hidden object behind the screen

layout.description: Testing desk with an opaque cloth curtain hiding tactile objects below a tachistoscope screen.

positions.where: seated at the desk reaching his left hand under the cloth curtain

props.name: opaque desk screen and hidden object tray
props.period_detail: wooden frame with grey cloth curtain concealing a spoon, key, pencil, and comb
props.physical_behavior: left hand feels behind the curtain and lifts the spoon flashed on the left screen

actions.verb_sequence: shakes his head saying he saw nothing -> slips his left hand behind the curtain and lifts the exact flashed spoon

reactions.reaction: exchange astonished looks as the silent right brain answers with the left hand

scenes.recognition_hook: Verbally swearing he saw nothing while his left hand picks up the exact object behind a curtain.

scenes.title: Everyday interpreter: spinning reasons for an impulse decision

layout.description: Bright modern living room desk with an impulse package delivery.

positions.where: holding an impulse gadget box while talking to a friend

props.name: unboxed gadget and checklist pad
props.period_detail: cardboard parcel and notepad listing post-hoc 'reasons'

actions.verb_sequence: opens the impulse box -> immediately gestures through a confident three-point justification

reactions.reaction: folds arms recognizing the classic post-hoc excuse

scenes.recognition_hook: Even with an intact corpus callosum, your left-brain interpreter still invents instant excuses for gut impulses.
